paragraphs: Friend, here's what Jeremiah 25 teaches me. God warns before He acts, and He doesn't stop at one warning. Twenty-three years of Jeremiah speaking, plus all His servants the prophets, again and again (Jeremiah 25:3-4). The call was simple: "Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways and deeds" (Jeremiah 25:5). Listening was never meant to be the hard part.

Now look at who God sends. He calls Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon "My servant" (Jeremiah 25:9). So even a mighty foreign king is not running loose. And when the seventy years are complete, God says He will punish the king of Babylon for the guilt of that land (Jeremiah 25:12). Nobody gets to say, "I'm the one in charge here," because God is the One who holds the calendar, and I mean ALL of it.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When God's word keeps coming, don't hit snooze on it. I've hit snooze on plenty of things, but never on something this clear. Hear it, turn, and trust that the God who set the seventy years is still the One who keeps His word, whether He is warning or promising.
